Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What is necessary for effective specialisation?

options.A: a barter system
options.B: a medium of exchange
options.C: a production possibility curve
options.D: a system of trade protection

questions.questionText: The change from WX to YZ in a country’s production possibility curve is shown. Y W food O X Z clothes What could have caused this shift?

options.A: an increase in employment among the existing labour force
options.B: an increase in the rate of interest
options.C: the closing of an inefficient factory
options.D: the discovery of a new resource

questions.questionText: Recently, thousands of ancient Roman coins were discovered buried in a field in the UK. Funds were raised by a museum to buy them. What function of money did the coins retain?

options.A: a medium of exchange
options.B: a standard for deferred payments
options.C: a store of value
options.D: a unit of account

questions.questionText: What describes a market supply curve?

options.A: It is downward sloping.
options.B: It is the same as the aggregate supply curve.
options.C: It is the sum of all firms’ supply curves for a product.
options.D: It is the supply of all products within an economy.

questions.questionText: The demand curve for new cars in a country shifted to the left. Which change could have caused such a shift?

options.A: an increase in real disposable income
options.B: an increase in the cost of borrowing
options.C: an increase in the price of new cars
options.D: an increase in the price of train travel

questions.questionText: The table gives estimates of the price elasticities and cross elasticities of demand for bus and rail travel. elasticity with respect to the price of service bus travel rail travel bus travel –0.37 +0.13 rail travel +0.16 –0.43 What would be the change in the volume of rail travel resulting from a 1% increase in bus fares?

options.A: an increase of 0.16%
options.B: an increase of 0.43%
options.C: a reduction of 0.13%
options.D: a reduction of 0.37%

questions.questionText: It has been estimated that bread has an income elasticity of –0.04. What can be concluded about bread from this information?

options.A: It is a normal good.
options.B: It is an inferior good.
options.C: It has many complements.
options.D: It has many substitutes.

questions.questionText: A US study, published in July 2014, warned teenagers to reduce the amount of fizzy drink they consume. One can of fizzy drink contains an adult’s entire daily sugar allowance. If the advice were accepted, how might the effect be illustrated on demand and supply diagrams for fizzy drinks and for sugar? diagram for fizzy drinks diagram for sugar

options.B: demand curve moves to the left movement down the supply curve
options.C: movement up the demand curve supply curve moves to the right
options.D: movement up the demand curve supply curve moves to the left

options.A: a shortage of applicants for rented housing
options.B: a shortage of rented housing
options.C: an increase in supply to satisfy the increased demand for rented housing
options.D: an increase in the number of occupants of rented housing

It also levies a sales tax of 10% on most products, although some essential goods are exempt. Which combination of tax changes is most likely to create a more equal distribution of income in the country? income tax sales tax

questions.questionText: A government decides to privatise a nationalised company by transferring ownership directly to its managers and workers. What is its most likely motive for this decision?

options.A: to increase the amount of innovation
options.B: to increase the level of competition
options.C: to increase the level of incentive
options.D: to increase the scale of production

questions.questionText: In 2012, high street shops reported a fall in sales as domestic demand in an economy fell. However, the impact on the overall economy was not as unfavourable as was first feared. What might have lessened the impact on the economy?

options.A: Exports increased.
options.B: Imports increased.
options.C: Savings increased.
options.D: Taxes increased.

A country experienced an annual deflation rate of 2% for four successive years. Which statement is correct for the four-year period?

options.A: The price level fell by 8%.
options.B: The price level fell by less than 8%.
options.C: The real value of money fell by 8%.
options.D: The real value of money fell by less than 8%.

questions.questionText: In July 2013, orders for durable US manufactured goods from computers to aircraft fell 7.3%, the biggest fall for a year. What might explain this change in trade and how would it have affected the US balance of payments? reason for change effect on balance of payments

options.A: an expansion in domestic production increased outflow in the current account
options.B: an expansion in foreign markets reduced inflow in the financial account
options.C: a recession in domestic production increased outflow in the financial account
options.D: a recession in foreign markets reduced inflow in the current account

options.A: £1=less than $0.50

options.C: £1=between $1 and $1.50
options.D: £1=more than $1.50

questions.questionText: What is not associated with greater economic integration between countries?

options.A: increased financial flows
options.B: increased quotas
options.C: increased trade creation
options.D: increased trade diversion

questions.questionText: Which statement is not a valid justification for an import tariff?

options.A: A tariff will prevent imported inflation.
options.B: A tariff will prevent unfair foreign competition.
options.C: A tariff will protect a developing industry.
options.D: A tariff will protect an industry in decline.

questions.questionText: An increase in interest rates is an example of which type of policy?

options.A: contractionary fiscal policy
options.B: contractionary monetary policy
options.C: expansionary monetary policy
options.D: restrictive supply-side policy

questions.questionText: Possible policies a government might use to reduce a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments include devaluation, government spending cuts, interest rate rises and tariffs. Which two policies would be classified as expenditure-reducing?

options.A: devaluation and government spending cuts
options.B: government spending cuts and interest rate rises
options.C: interest rate rises and tariffs
options.D: tariffs and devaluation

questions.questionText: Which policy, adopted by a government with the intention of reducing the rate of inflation, might cause a greater deficit on the balance of payments?

options.A: higher foreign exchange rates for its currency
options.B: higher interest rates for domestic customers
options.C: higher subsidies to domestic producers
